name: Cardenas hydrophilic-catheter SCI trial
question: Does a hydrophilic-coated intermittent catheter delay symptomatic urinary tract infection compared with an uncoated catheter after acute traumatic spinal cord injury?

arms.label: single-use uncoated polyvinyl chloride Conveen catheter

design.population: 224 intermittent-catheter users with traumatic spinal cord injury less than three months old were recruited at 15 North American spinal cord injury centers.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Design, Setting, Participants and Methods

verdictNote: First treated symptomatic UTI was delayed; institutional-period UTI incidence was lower.
takeaway: In acute traumatic spinal cord injury, single-use hydrophilic-coated SpeediCath delayed the first antibiotic-treated symptomatic urinary tract infection compared with an uncoated Conveen catheter; daily first-infection risk was 33% lower and institutional-period antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI incidence was 21% lower.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Cardenas DD, Moore KN, Dannels-McClure A, et al. "Intermittent Catheterization With a Hydrophilic-Coated Catheter Delays Urinary Tract Infections in Acute Spinal Cord Injury: A Prospective, Randomized, Multicenter Trial." *PM R.* 2011;3(5):408-417. doi:10.1016/j.pmrj.2011.01.001
reports.followUp: During hospitalization or rehabilitation and up to three months after discharge; maximum six months.

results.endpoint: Time to first antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI
results.measure: Daily risk of first antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI; relative reduction
results.note: The abstract reports a significant delay but no absolute event counts, hazard ratio, confidence interval or exact P value.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Main Outcome Measurements and Results

results.endpoint: Antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI incidence during institutional care
results.measure: Institutional-period symptomatic UTI incidence; relative reduction
results.note: The abstract gives a relative reduction without group-specific counts or rates.

delivery.label: Catheter assignment
delivery.note: Randomization occurred within ten days of starting intermittent catheterization.
